observation.visible_scene: A horizontal clear glass tube is held at its midpoint by a metal clamp on a vertical stand, with two blue plastic stoppers fixed on the tube near the clamp. Each open end of the tube is sealed by an orange cap containing a white cotton-like plug. A faint white vapor/cloud is visible inside the right half of the tube. The background is a black board on a white wall; two blue screw caps sit on the table at the bottom. A thin transparent rod/stem enters from the upper-right, its tip reaching into the tube near the right cotton plug.
visible_changes: The transparent rod at the right end gradually shifts rightward and rotates toward horizontal over the first ~14 frames (t=0 to ~0.87 s), then is no longer visible from frame 15 onward, i.e. it is withdrawn out of the tube to the right.

A white vapor mass occupying the right portion of the tube slowly creeps/expands leftward and becomes slightly more diffuse across the whole excerpt; its leading edge moves from roughly the tube's right-center toward a bit further left, but never reaches the left cotton plug.

All other elements remain fixed: the stand, clamp, blue tube stoppers, both cotton plugs, the orange end caps, the two table caps, and the blackboard framing are unchanged in position, indicating a static camera with no panning or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: The origin or cause of the white vapor is not shown (no onset, injection, or reaction is captured within the segment).
What the rod was used for, and whether it was inserted or merely held, is unknown; its motion before t=0 and any action after t=2.67 s are outside the crop.
The identities of the vapors/materials and the purpose of the apparatus are not determinable from these frames.
uncertain_details: Whether the slight leftward advance of the vapor is genuine drift or partly a lighting/contrast effect is hard to confirm frame-by-frame.
The exact geometry of the rod relative to the tube (inside vs. resting at the opening) is ambiguous due to transparency and reflections.
Camera motion is assumed negligible based on consistent background edges, but cannot be fully verified.
